question_text: A network technician replaced an access layer switch and needs to reconfigure it to allow the connected devices to connect to the correct networks.
explanation: Switch 1 Ports 1 and 2 must remain enabled with LACP enabled and VLANs 1, 60, 90, 120, and 220 tagged. Switch 1 Ports 5 and 6 must carry VLANs 60, 120, and 150 as tagged uplinks to Switch 2. Switch 1 Ports 7 and 8 plus Switch 3 Ports 1 and 2 must form the fault-tolerant LACP connection with VLANs 60, 90, 120, and 220 tagged. Switch 3 Ports 3 and 5 must be disabled. Switch 3 Port 4 must carry VLAN 120 and 220 as tagged for the VoIP phone and PC3. Switch 3 Port 6 must be VLAN 120 untagged, Port 7 VLAN 60 untagged, and Port 8 VLAN 90 untagged.

instructions: Click on the appropriate port(s) on Switch 1 and Switch 3 to verify or reconfigure the correct settings:
Ensure each device accesses only its correctly associated network.
Disable all unused switchports.
Require fault-tolerant connections between the switches.
Only make necessary changes to complete the above requirements.
If at any time you would like to bring back the initial state of the simulation, please click the Reset All button.

question_text: A network technician was recently onboarded to a company. A manager has tasked the technician with documenting the network and has provided the technician with partial information from previous documentation.
explanation: Use the Core Switch 1 ARP data together with the MAC address tables on Access Switch 1 and Access Switch 2. The documented result is that PC1, PC2, and PC3 belong to VLAN 10, while PC4 belongs to VLAN 20. The partial fields shown in the PDF are completed by correlating the ARP entries with the switchport learn tables.

question_text: Users are unable to access files on their department share located on file server 2. The network administrator has been tasked with validating routing between networks hosting workstation A and file server 2.
explanation: Router A must be marked Yes and configured with destination prefix 10.0.5.0, mask 255.255.255.0, interface Gi1. Router B must be marked Yes and configured with destination prefix 10.0.1.0, mask 255.255.255.0, interface Gi2. Router C must remain No because its /22 routes already cover the required networks.

instructions: Click on each router to review output, identify any issues, and configure the appropriate solution.
If at any time you would like to bring back the initial state of the simulation, please click the Reset All button.

question_text: A network administrator has been tasked with configuring a network for a new corporate office. The office consists of two buildings, separated by 50 feet with no physical connectivity. The configuration must meet the following requirements:
explanation: The PDF accepts Switch on the left side of Building A, Firewall at the top center, Router beneath the Firewall, and the WAP and Wireless range extender in the two remaining wireless positions. The lecture notes explicitly allow either WAP-right plus extender-bottom or extender-right plus WAP-bottom.

instructions: Devices in both buildings should be able to access the Internet.
Security insists that all Internet traffic be inspected before entering the network.
Desktops should not see traffic destined for other devices.
Select the appropriate network device for each location. If applicable, click on the magnifying glass next to any device which may require configuration updates and make any necessary changes.
Not all devices will be used, but all locations should be filled.
If at any time you would like to bring back the initial state of the simulation, please click the Reset All button.

question_text: A network technician needs to resolve some issues with a customer's SOHO network. The customer reports that some of the devices are not connecting to the network, while others appear to work as intended.
explanation: The unambiguous issues visible in the PDF are Cable 2 exceeding 100 meters, Cable 5 using crossover wiring, Cable 4 on the wrong VLAN, Cable 7 on the wrong VLAN, Cable 8 on the wrong VLAN, and the printer using 10.10.11.56 instead of the documented 10.10.11.16. The PDF notes also mention possible gateway and DNS issues, but those are not fully evidenced by the provided screenshots.

instructions: Troubleshoot all the network components and review the cable test results by clicking on each device and cable.
Type help in each terminal to view a list of available commands.
Diagnose the appropriate component(s) by identifying any components with a problem and recommend a solution to correct each problem.
If at any time you would like to bring back the initial state of the simulation, please click the Reset All button.

question_text: After a recent power outage, users are reporting performance issues accessing the application servers. Wireless users are also reporting intermittent Internet issues.
explanation: WAN2 should be preferred for VoIP because it has significantly lower jitter than WAN1. Router A is the device timing out in the device status panel. In the Top Hosts widget, 10.1.90.53 is the highest-volume workstation address even though 206.208.133.9 is the overall top host.

instructions: Click on each tab at the top of the screen.
Select a widget to view information, then use the drop-down menus to answer the associated questions.
If at any time you would like to bring back the initial state of the simulation, please click the Reset All button.
